subject: Post-call technical brief: Velocity Systems latency & topology alignment
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kiran Shah <kiran@velocitysys.com>, Maya Li <maya.li@velocitysys.com>
Cc: Prıyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call technical brief: Velocity Systems latency & topology alignment

Hi Kiran & Maya —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap of what we heard, confirmed actions, and a proposed next-step plan so we’re aligned before the SOW discussion: 

Pain points we heard
- Inference latency spikes during peak retail traffic (5-7pm PT window) causing timeouts in the personalization pipeline.
- Current self-hosted stack cannot sustain 200 concurrent streaming requests without >500ms tail latency.
- Ops team lacks visibility into token-level cost and fallback behavior when GPU capacity is constrained.

Goals you stated
- 95th percentile token latency <= 200ms for single-turn personalization responses at 200 rps sustained.
- Predictable monthly cost envelope with soft cap alerts.
- Ability to run canary model variants and automatic fallback to a quantized, lower-cost model when primary capacity is saturated.

My read on model/deployment requirements
- Primary model: ~7B mixed-precision transformer, streaming enabled.
- Secondary fallback: 3B quantized variant (int8) for graceful degradation.
- KV-cache reuse across sessions is critical (prefix patterns are similar across users).

Technical next steps (owners & timeline)
1) Redwood to deliver a proposed topology diagram + expected latency/cost estimates by EOD Wed (attachment: topology-diagram.v1.png) — owner: Rishi.
2) Velocity to provide a 48-hour trace sample from the 5-7pm window and a CSV of request size / token distribution — owner: Kiran — due: Mon 5/24.
3) Follow-up technical deep-dive with infra + ops (30–45m) to walk through canary & fallback policies — propose Thu 5/20 11am PT — owners: Evelyn / Priyom.

Attachments included: redwood-sla-delta-proposal.pdf (draft SLA deltas for canary/fallback), topology-diagram.v1.png (initial sketch).

If that looks right I’ll get the calendar invite out for Thu and Rishi will attach the latency/cost estimates.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com | M: (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

Subject: Re: Post-call technical brief: Velocity Systems latency & topology alignment

Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear recap. Confirming the facts on our side: 
- Peak window is 17:00–19:00 PT, primarily East/West coast users.
- We saw tail latencies up to ~1.2s on instances handling concurrent streaming personalization requests (these are multi-turn sessions but single request per eval).
- Average request size: 700 tokens in, ~120 tokens generated; 95% of sessions reuse the same prefix (customer profile) across the session.

We’ll upload the 48-hour trace + token distribution CSV to the Drive link you shared by EOD Mon. 

Quick question: when you reference "soft cap alerts" — do you have a default alerting cadence we can mirror (e.g., 80% capacity sustained for 5m)? If Rishi can put recommended thresholds in his topology doc that’d be great.

Maya & I can do the deep-dive Thu 5/20 11am PT — confirmed from our side. 

Thanks,
Kiran Shah
Head of ML Infrastructure
Velocity Systems

Subject: Re: Post-call technical brief: Velocity Systems latency & topology alignment

Evelyn / team —

Attaching the initial topology sketch and a short table of latency and cost estimates based on the stats Kiran shared on the call. Notes: 
- Assumptions: primary model ~7B, fp16; fallback ~3B int8; traffic profile: 200 sustained rps, 2x spike headroom.
- Expected 95th percentile token latency on a single A100-equivalent GPU with continuous batching and KV-cache hit rate ~70%: ~120–180ms depending on sequence length distribution.
- For graceful fallback we recommend: warm standby pool of quantized instances (3–5% of steady-state capacity) + autoscale policy that triggers fallback at sustained 85% GPU utilization for 3m.
- Cost: projected token compute cost delta vs your current environment: ~22–28% reduction at steady state with Redwood batching + prefix caching.

Attachments referenced below (uploaded to the Drive link): topology-diagram.v1.png, redwood-sla-delta-proposal.pdf. I included recommended alert thresholds inline: 80% sustained 5m (warning), 90% sustained 3m (auto-fallback).

I’ll drop a short one-page latency/cost summary into the HubSpot record after you both review.

—Rishi
